title: Song of Solomon 3:6–11
context: The scene shifts to a procession. A voice asks who is coming up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, fragrant with myrrh and frankincense, and the answer is Solomon’s carriage, guarded by sixty mighty men with swords against dangers in the night. The carriage is described as made by King Solomon from the wood of Lebanon, with pillars of silver, a base of gold, and a seat of purple; the phrase paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem, is obscure, and translations and interpreters render it in different ways. The daughters of Zion are called to see King Solomon wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding. The WEB gives no speaker label here, and interpreters variously assign the lines to the Friends, a chorus, or the Beloved. The passage is commonly read first as a description of a royal wedding procession. A typological reading, common in both Arminian and Reformed traditions, also hears in it the coming of Christ the King for his bride (compare Isaiah 61:10; Revelation 19:7), and many readers hold the two together.

verses.text: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see someone coming up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, fragrant with myrrh and frankincense. The scene builds anticipation.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see a description of a splendid approach. Some figurative readers recall Israel’s wilderness journey, and some hear the church coming to her Lord, readings found in both traditions.

verses.text: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Solomon’s carriage surrounded by sixty mighty men of Israel. The scene displays royal honor and protection.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the guard as a sign of security and dignity. Readers in both traditions commonly read the verse first as description of a royal procession.

verses.text: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the guards skilled with the sword, ready because of fear in the night. Love and celebration are protected from danger.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see watchful protection around the procession. Figurative readers sometimes hear the security God provides for his people, held alongside the literal reading.

verses.text: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see King Solomon making a carriage of the wood of Lebanon. The detail highlights craftsmanship and splendor.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see royal provision and care (compare 1 Kings 5:6). Readers in both traditions commonly appreciate the description without requiring a symbolic meaning for each material.

verses.text: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see pillars of silver, a base of gold, a seat of purple, and an interior described as paved with love. Splendor and love belong together.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see rich materials honoring the occasion. Readers in both traditions commonly hold the obscure phrase about love from the daughters of Jerusalem with caution.

verses.text: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the daughters of Zion called to see King Solomon crowned on the day of his wedding and gladness. Marriage is a time of joy.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see marriage celebrated as a good gift. A common typological reading in both traditions hears Christ’s joy in his bride (compare Isaiah 62:5; Revelation 19:7).
